summary: US-F4: The settlement ledger attributes every fee cent to a payee
description:
**As** a platform operator, **I want** a captured order to land as ledger entries that name every
payee and account for every cent, **so that** settlement is a read of recorded fact rather than a
recomputation.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-215, TKT-216

The other half of TKT-6's second COS: *the settlement ledger attributes every fee cent to a payee;
splits sum exactly to totals*. ADR-002 puts the settlement ledger in `payments`, next to the
append-only money journal.

**Two traps worth naming up front.** First, **absorbed fees still have to balance**: the buyer paid
face value, the payee is owed a fee out of it, so the organizer's line is face value *minus* the
absorbed fee. A ledger that only records passed-on fees balances against the charge and is wrong
about who earned what. Second, **capture is replayed** — ADR-016's recovery path re-runs a
checkout that may already have captured, so entry writing is idempotent or the ledger double-counts.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A migration adds settlement entries to payments: scoped to the organizer and the captured
  order/fact, naming the payee, an entry kind (face value vs fee), the fee code where applicable,
  amount and currency. **Append-only**, enforced the same way `journal_entries` enforces it — a
  trigger that raises on UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE.
- [ ] Entries are written **in the same transaction** as the capture's journal append (ADR-003 /
  ADR-011). A capture that journals but does not settle, or settles twice, is not a state this
  system can reach.
- [ ] **Sum-exactness is proven, not asserted in prose**: for a captured order, the entries sum
  exactly to the captured amount. A test constructs a deliberately unbalanced set and shows it is
  refused. State plainly — and test — whether the refusal is a database constraint or an
  application check, and why that is the right level.
- [ ] Absorbed fees are recorded as a payee credit against a reduced organizer line, so the buyer's
  total is untouched **and** the ledger still balances. A test asserts both halves at once: same
  captured amount, different entry set, exact sum.
- [ ] Idempotent under replay: re-running a capture that already settled writes nothing new and
  changes no amount (ADR-016's recovery path is the fixture, not a hand-rolled second call).
- [ ] The entries for an order are readable through a contract-declared internal response; regen
  committed.
- [ ] The integrity claim **names its adversary** (ADR-021). Either the entries join the journal's
  hash chain and the claim is tamper-evidence, or they do not and the claim is honest-writer
  consistency. Say which, in the ADR/ledger comment, in the words ADR-021 uses. Do not write
  "tamper-evident" about state a database writer can edit.
- [ ] `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS, gateway smoke suite); regenerated code committed before the gate runs (ADR-009).

**Non-goals:** settlement reports, per-event rollups and exports (TKT-23) · payout execution
(not in this epic) · fee/settlement reversal on refund, exchange and cancellation (carved out to a
follow-up; see the epic readiness verdict) · the back-office settlement page (TKT-23 owns it, and
ADR-042 records that its route must be added to the role matrix when it lands).

objective.note: Every captured cent is attributed to a payee in an append-only ledger, and the attribution is provably exact.

scope.note: Payments: schema + write at capture + one internal read. Commerce hands over the resolved split it already computed; it does not re-resolve.

uncertainties.note: Whether the split travels on the existing charge call or a separate internal call, and whether entries chain into the journal hash (which decides the ADR-021 wording). Both are plan-stage calls; the ACs constrain either answer.

dependencies.note: Blocked by TKT-215 (the breakdown to settle) and TKT-216 (the allocator that turns it into payee parts).

approach.note: Follow journal_entries: append-only trigger, organizer scoping, one transaction with the money fact. The recovery runner is the replay fixture.

first_slice.note: Last slice - it consumes both predecessors and is the COS's visible end.

success.note: Exact-sum, refusal and idempotency assertions, all deterministic.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code - floats are banned on money paths.

Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate - `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

governingAdrs.why: SHIPPED BY TKT-216 AND THIS TICKET'S DIRECT INPUT. The allocator (services/payments/internal/splits.Allocate) is already written and tested: largest remainder, exact sum, ties on payee id, never forms amount*share_bps, and VALIDATES ITS OWN INPUT because this ticket hands it persisted snapshots. §5 records two integrity escapes review found in the balance triggers - a moved part validating only its destination, and TRUNCATE firing no row trigger - so do not assume a stored schedule is balanced; the allocator re-checks and so must you.

The fee model. §2: a resolved fee of amount 0 is STILL a fee and must appear - so a payee can legitimately be owed zero, and that is different from absent. §3: incidence decides who bears it, and an ABSORBED fee is still owed to a payee out of money the buyer already paid, which is the case most likely to be got wrong here.

Every money mutation flows through the append-only journal. Settlement entries are money state and inherit that discipline - journal_entries' trigger refusing UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE is the pattern to COPY, not to reinvent (TKT-216 shipped that exact hole by writing a new guard from first principles).
The checkout journal protocol fixes what is written at capture and in which transaction. Settlement entries join that transaction or they can diverge from the money fact.

Checkout recovery REPLAYS a capture whose outcome is unknown. Entry writing must be idempotent under that replay, and the recovery runner is the fixture that proves it - not a hand-rolled second call.

Name the adversary before writing 'tamper-evident'. State inside the database cannot constrain an adversary who writes to the database. Either the entries join the journal's hash chain and the claim is tamper-evidence, or they do not and it is honest-writer consistency. Say which.
payments owns the settlement ledger. catalog owns the rules; commerce composes the money. This ticket must not move that line.
The PSP port: the captured amount is what the provider confirmed. The ledger settles THAT number, never a recomputation.
Contract-first; regen committed before the gate.
Migrations run out-of-band via each binary's migrate subcommand.

reference.summary: Epic lineage and the three epic-level COS
THE ALLOCATOR IS ALREADY BUILT - use it, do not rewrite it
The append-only pattern to copy verbatim, including the TRUNCATE guard

What commerce persists and this ticket settles from: {resolution, breakdown, face_value, passed_on_fees, absorbed_fees, total_amount}; breakdown items are {fee_code, basis, incidence, amount, currency}; the resolution carries each code's split with payee parts
The capture path and its idempotency registry

TKT-215 closeout: refunds under-refund by the passed-on fee, and the fee-on-exchange policy was decided by an agent as 'carried'. Both are things this ledger will eventually have to reverse and neither is decided
TKT-216 closeout: two integrity escapes got through a deferred-trigger design; distrust 'the database enforces it' without reading how far it goes

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-217 (US-F4)

**Selection.** The last child of TKT-6, and now the only claimable one. Both blockers closed.

**Blockers verified:** `blocked-by TKT-215` — resolved (`f1d5f44f`). `blocked-by TKT-216` — resolved
(`43fdd0f5`). Zero open.

**Branch:** `TKT-217-settlement-ledger`, cut from `origin/main` at `ac550399`.

**Risk verdict — `risk:low` NOT claimed.** This ticket writes the ledger that says who is owed what.
It touches the capture transaction, adds append-only money state, and makes an integrity claim. Money
path, data migration, and an audit-trail assertion all apply — this is the highest-risk ticket of the
four, and it is the one whose mistakes are least recoverable: a misattributed cent stays
misattributed.

**Gates waived — same terms as TKT-214/215/216**, restated so this ticket stands alone: Gate 1 by the
owner's instruction; Gate 2 by agent judgement after the cross-model critique; Gate 3 by agent
squash-merge after the ai-review converges under the churn cap, review-guide first; Gate 4 by
self-validation against test evidence on merged code.

**Model routing** re-read at claim, unchanged: `plan` = `gpt-5.6-luna` · `planReview` = `main-agent` ·
`implement` = `main-agent` · `aiReview` = `gpt-5.6-luna`.

**Context-mémo re-baked**, and this one carries more than ADRs:

- **ADR-047 leads** — the allocator is **already written and tested**. This ticket consumes
  `splits.Allocate`; it does not reimplement it.
- **ADR-003 flagged with a specific instruction**: copy `journal_entries`' append-only trigger,
  including its TRUNCATE guard. TKT-216 shipped exactly that hole by writing a new guard from first
  principles while the battle-tested one sat in this same service. That is the "prior art" retro item
  from TKT-216, applied to the next ticket rather than filed and forgotten.
- **Both predecessors' closeouts are references**, because they carry facts no code shows: refunds
  currently under-refund by the passed-on fee, the fee-on-exchange policy was chosen by an agent as
  "carried", and a deferred-trigger design had two escapes. All three bear on what this ledger must
  eventually reverse.

**Applying TKT-216's process wins:** the `agent:plan-review` label moves **before** the critique, and
I will run `golangci-lint` plus every module's tests before invoking the gate.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Execution plan — TKT-217 (draft)

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna` (Codex, read-only, effort=high)**, per `config.models.plan`. Condensed.

#### 1. Entry model and arithmetic

`payments.settlement_entries`, one immutable row per line: organizer, order, `capture_fact_id`,
account role (`organizer`|`payee`), payee identity **snapshotted** so later catalog edits cannot
change historical settlement, `entry_kind` (`face_value`|`fee`), `fee_code` + `incidence` on fee
rows, amount, currency.

    organizer face entry = F − A
    fee entries          = allocated parts of every fee
    sum = (F − A) + P + A = F + P = C

Worked: face 5000, passed-on 600, absorbed 400, captured 5600 → organizer 4600 · venue/booking 360 ·
artist/booking 240 · system/service (absorbed) 400 · **total 5600**.

Uses the existing `splits.Allocate`; includes zero-valued parts (ADR-046 §2). *"Reject if `A > F`,
`C != snapshot.total_amount`, currencies differ, or any fee cannot be allocated."*

#### 2. Boundary and transaction

catalog resolves · commerce composes and persists the snapshot · **payments allocates and owns the
ledger**. Commerce sends a contract-declared settlement projection **derived from the persisted
snapshot, never a fresh catalog read**.

The draft then proposes restructuring capture: validate+allocate before the PSP, persist the plan on
`payment_operations`, and one transaction that locks the operation, appends `payment.captured`,
inserts entries and completes the operation — *"introduce a transaction-aware capture/finalization
method rather than composing independent calls"*, because `Journal.Append` owns its own transaction
and the handler appends before `CompleteOperation`.

#### 3. Sum-exactness at two levels

Application validation before any PSP call (catches `ErrUnbalanced`, `unsplit`, currency mismatch,
provider-amount mismatch) **and** a deferred constraint trigger validating the whole set at commit
(catches missing/extra rows, direct SQL, and application bugs that bypass the builder). *"A per-row
CHECK cannot validate a set sum."* Aggregate in `numeric` to avoid a `bigint` sum overflow. Copy the
append-only pattern from `0001_journal.sql` **including the statement-level TRUNCATE trigger**.

#### 4. Replay

Adds a provider-neutral `FinalizeCapture` to the recovery payments port and HTTP client, called from
the charge path, on replay, in `confirmation_pending` recovery, and after `payment_unknown` resolves.
Idempotent: matching rows → no writes; missing rows → repair only if the stored plan matches;
conflicting plan → fail closed; never a second PSP call.

#### 5. Integrity claim

**Do not** add settlement rows to the journal hash chain in this ticket. The claim is
**honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence** — an adversary with payments DB access can drop
triggers. Record it in a new ADR; never describe the entries as tamper-evident.

#### 6–9. DoD, files, tests

ADR-048 · payments migration `0004` · store/api/settlement changes · **PSP port + fake + Stripe
adapter** for a provider-confirmed captured amount · commerce `server.go`, `recovery/runner.go`,
`recovery/clients.go` · five smoke files.

Tests to observe failing first: absorbed-fee entry build (organizer 4600, fees 1000, total 5600) ·
unbalanced persisted split refused **before the PSP**, asserting no PSP call, no journal row, no
settlement row · unbalanced set refused at commit, with a fixture whose *only* failing condition is
the balance trigger · append-only UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE each separately · zero fee still names every
payee · `unsplit` fails closed · provider-amount mismatch fails closed · recovery finalizes before
confirm · replay of a settled capture is a no-op.
